title: Honest Intervals for Cumulative Incidence Contrasts under Discrete Censored-History Fusion
banked_reason: D0.5 delivered incremental below field, score ceiling 6.3 < 7.4, not salvageable in scope; independent validity gate confirms stopping and preserves an unresolved censoring-identification defect. Informal draft, not mathematically certified.
gap_reasons: The contribution beyond established [Li–Luedtke fusion theory](https://arxiv.org/html/2111.14945v4) and [Kabaila–Giri interval optimization](https://arxiv.org/html/0711.3236) is the certified full-box Gaussian width optimization and its explicit transfer counterexample; the finite-row gradient and count expansion are supporting specializations. The proved optimum concerns diagnostic-dependent symmetric widths around a fixed, prespecified pretest center, and its original-record converse covers the stated regular or controlled-convergent implementations rather than all confidence procedures. The prime-size construction disproves unrestricted transfer through exact rational decoding in a one-period equality experiment, but establishes neither the unrestricted optimum nor a practical improvement for longitudinal history fusion. The framing explicitly maintains these restrictions, so there is no stale claim of unrestricted optimality or an unresolved theorem presented as proved. The projected score is constrained by the absence of an evaluated multihistory primal-dual certificate or reproducible interval comparison demonstrating meaningful gains, together with insufficient theorem-level positioning against existing expected-length optimization methods. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.3 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

The claimed certified, implementable frontier is only asserted as an LP "specified in the proof"; lift the finite program's inputs, variables, constraints, and certified output into this theorem or def:frontier-handle so the headline deliverable is directly evaluable.

The theorem-level novelty claim lacks a precise comparison to the closest uncertain-prior/selective-inference and robust-borrowing results: state what their object, honesty regime, and lower-bound/optimization scope are, and exactly which asserted Gaussian/regular-frontier result is new.

Position the exact-lattice counterexample as a theorem-level boundary against a named prior Gaussian/regular-transfer claim, rather than only as an internally reciprocal companion; the current related-work text omits relevance treatment for some cited borrowing/prior-information sources and gives no closest-result comparison here.

proof_attempt_summary: The fixed-margin implementation angle was replaced by a local diagnostic-width program, producing informal Gaussian primal-dual certificates, strict-gain and regular-transfer results, and a prime-size exact-lattice counterexample to unrestricted transfer. D0.5 delivered incremental below the field floor (score ceiling 6.3 < 7.4), while independent review found the written marginal gate assumption insufficient for causal identification despite the latest panel math pass. Source attestations and all review receipts are preserved; no F-stage or Lean certification occurred, and any future re-raise requires an explicit stronger sequential observation regime plus fresh scientific and novelty review.
tldr: For a causal trial treatment-policy cause-1 incidence contrast, the finite censored-history model yields a signed canonical gradient, exact nodewise fusion gain, and a uniform same-sample diagnostic experiment. The two frontier theorems give one resolved boundary: computable primal-dual certificates are sharp for Gaussian diagnostic kernels and regular or controlled-convergent original-record implementations, while an explicit bounded, uniformly honest prime-size exact-lattice rule beats the Gaussian value and refutes unrestricted diagnostic lower transfer.
gap: Su et al. leaves cumulative-incidence test-then-pool estimation and history adjustment as future directions. Yang et al. already supplies pretest local laws and conservative coverage; a normal approximation after compatibility selection is not a new principle. The uncomputed object is the sharp diagnostic-dependent expected-length frontier for the history-node causal experiment.
fill: The signed finite-history score geometry determines the local experiment. A fully specified pretest estimator and an honest constant-width fallback support a probability-kernel optimization with feasible upper certificates and dual lower certificates. The optimization and its attainable original-record length bound are the new open content.
